qualifying_findings.title: Docker MCP Gateway OCI label parsing allows docker run argument injection

visible_dates.source: GitHub release page visible release date

qualifying_findings.qualification_basis: CVE publication and update timestamps are inside the collector window; the GitHub advisory and release are older provenance and patch evidence.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record plus maintainer advisory and patch/release references
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-55887 reports that Docker MCP Gateway versions from 0.21.0 before 0.42.2 unmarshalled attacker-controlled OCI image label YAML into a broad server structure. Runtime fields such as volumes, user, command, extra hosts, allow-hosts, network, environment, remote endpoint, OAuth, secrets, long-lived mode, and policy could reach container launch behavior. The GitHub advisory describes host-impacting arbitrary code execution when a malicious image injects docker run arguments such as host filesystem or docker socket mounts.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: docker/mcp-gateway >= 0.21.0 and < 0.42.2; patched in 0.42.2 according to advisory and release references.
qualifying_findings.security_delta: New CVE publication for an MCP runtime supply-chain flaw where metadata from a referenced image can reshape local container execution.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP gateways mediate AI agent tools. Treating image metadata as trusted runtime configuration can let a tool source cross the agent-to-host boundary and gain host access, so MCP catalog and image provenance need strict allowlisting and origin separation.

upstream_routing.routing_note: Keep broad Docker/MCP Gateway product coverage upstream; local ingest should retain the image-metadata trust boundary, affected versions, patch, and agent-host execution implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE publication timing and affected range from CVE Services; GitHub advisory page is older than the window but corroborates impact and patched version.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, map this to MCP supply-chain and hosted MCP runtime security leaves.
Recheck whether local pages already have a Docker MCP Gateway or MCP gateway security lens before creating a new leaf.
Capture patch reference v0.42.2 and note that older advisory/release dates should not be treated as new September disclosures.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-searxng web_url_read allows DNS-resolved private-hostname SSRF
qualifying_findings.qualification_basis: CVE publication and update timestamps are inside the collector window; the GitHub advisory is older corroborating primary detail.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record plus maintainer advisory with proof-of-concept details
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-58485 reports that mcp-searxng before 1.7.1 validates only the literal hostname in web_url_read before the fetch layer performs operating-system DNS resolution. A public-looking attacker-controlled hostname that resolves to private, loopback, link-local, or cloud metadata addresses can pass the policy check and make the MCP server read internal HTTP resources. The GitHub advisory states that default HTTP mode lacks authentication and that STDIO exploitation can occur when an AI agent is induced to call the tool with attacker-controlled URLs.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-searxng < 1.7.1; patched in 1.7.1 according to CVE and GitHub advisory references.
qualifying_findings.security_delta: New CVE publication for SSRF in an MCP web-reading tool, with DNS rebinding/private-address bypass detail.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Web-reading tools are common AI-agent capabilities. If prompt injection or malicious page content can steer an agent into a crafted URL, the MCP server may become a bridge from untrusted web content to internal services, secrets, or cloud metadata.

upstream_routing.routing_note: Keep broad MCP server catalog coverage upstream; local ingest should retain the SSRF, DNS-resolution, tool-authentication, and prompt-injection exploitability implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE timing and vulnerable range from CVE Services; GitHub advisory provides older but detailed primary proof and mitigation context.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, deduplicate against any existing MCP SSRF/private-network leaf or create a focused MCP web-reading SSRF note.
Record default HTTP authentication posture and STDIO prompt-injection pathway as separate deployment-boundary considerations.
Recheck release v1.7.1 for final remediation wording.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise MongoDBMemory NoSQL injection leaks cross-session chat history
qualifying_findings.qualification_basis: CVE publication and update timestamps are inside the collector window; the GitHub advisory is older corroborating primary detail.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vulnerability record plus maintainer advisory and external advisory reference
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-91937 reports that Flowise before 3.1.4 fails to sanitize overrideConfig.sessionId before using it in MongoDBMemory queries. Unauthenticated attackers can send MongoDB operator objects through the prediction API and read chat-history records for other users from the shared collection. The GitHub advisory describes the issue as a cross-session data leak through public chatflows and recommends coercing the session identifier to a string before it reaches the MongoDB query.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise versions before 3.1.4; 3.1.4 listed as unaffected in CVE Services.
qualifying_findings.security_delta: New CVE publication for an AI workflow product data-isolation flaw affecting chat memory confidentiality.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI agent and chatflow memory can contain API keys, passwords, internal configuration, and sensitive user prompts. Session isolation failures turn shared memory backends into data-exposure risks even when the model layer is behaving as intended.

upstream_routing.routing_note: Keep broad Flowise product/framework coverage upstream; local ingest should retain the chat-memory isolation, unauthenticated prediction API, and sensitive prompt/data leakage implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE timing and affected version from CVE Services; GitHub advisory is archived/older but contains detailed primary exploit chain.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, connect this to AI data security/privacy and agent memory isolation leaves.
Recheck whether the Flowise repository archive status affects remediation availability or migration guidance.
Treat the GitHub advisory's 'No known CVE' display as stale against the newer CVE Services publication.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI publicly backs stronger UK frontier AI rules while parliamentary committee seeks independent oversight
qualifying_findings.qualification_basis: Article publication timestamp is inside the collector window and reports concrete proposed governance controls for high-risk/frontier AI systems.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable public secondary reporting on policy and governance controls
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: The Guardian reported that OpenAI urged UK lawmakers to legislate for the most powerful AI labs, while a UK parliamentary human-rights committee called for a new AI bill, mandatory transparency requirements, and an independent oversight body with enforcement power. The article also notes that the UK AI Security Institute currently tests advanced models but lacks power to compel developers such as Anthropic to submit systems for scrutiny.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: UK frontier AI governance and advanced model oversight; not a software version.
qualifying_findings.security_delta: In-window public policy signal for mandatory transparency, independent oversight, and stronger authority over advanced AI testing.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The item changes the governance and assurance discussion from voluntary frontier-lab safety practices toward enforceable oversight, testing access, and evidence requirements for high-risk AI systems.
named_entities: UK Parliament Joint Committee on Human Rights

upstream_routing.routing_note: Keep broad OpenAI, Anthropic, and UK AI Act/policy entity coverage upstream; local ingest should retain the assurance, model-testing authority, transparency, and security-governance implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Moderate confidence: article has clear visible dates and named actors, but primary committee text and OpenAI statement should be located during ingest before durable synthesis.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, locate the UK committee primary report or bill text before writing durable governance claims.
